judgements.justification: A's Reviewer_N9bU wrongly read the theory as relying on binary decision variables, but the experimental half of the claim was right and N9bU still raised to 7, so the error held no score down.
B's chair gave an oral on four 7s and one thinly argued 9, a tier above what the ratings and arguments supported.
B's Reviewer_rfa1 gave a 'top 15%' 9 on three generic sentences of praise, and the chair quoted that praise; B's confidence-1 reviewers nWYc and 4Bw1 also gave unsupported 7s.
No flaw was disclosed on one forum only; each concession answers that committee's own reviewers.
No committee ignored a substantive flaw; A weighed its clarity concerns, and B never learned of the cut-off Definition 2.2.
The rebuttal raised scores in both committees: N9bU in A, and 1SfX and 3m9X in B.
Only A raised the cut-off Definition 2.2, the wrong error metric and the unlabelled axis, which fed A's clarity verdict; only B raised the strict exact-imitation target and graph misspecification.
Both committees saw dense notation; A's chair named clarity the main shortcoming, while B's chair mentioned no weakness and called the paper clear.
B's chair stated no own assessment and quoted rfa1's strengths paragraph verbatim, so rfa1's 9 set the oral; A's chair also copied N9bU's summary.
No score moved because of other reviews; the raises cite the rebuttal.
1SfX got no answer on the HighD graph's realism but still raised to 7; no score was held down by a missed reply.
rfa1's 9 rested on assertion, was posted two weeks late, and rfa1 never joined the discussion, yet it counted unchallenged and lifted B's mean from 7.0 to 7.4.
Neither chair went below its reviewers' ratings.
Neither chair stated a positive view and then deferred to a threshold on the mean.
No below-threshold score remains; A's lowest is a 6 in the accept range.
Both committees read the paper as a theoretical causal criterion for imitation learning.
A's Reviewer_N9bU, at confidence 1, raised to accept on the rebuttal's framing and the promised de Haan citation, without new results or a proof check.
Both committees asked the same of the paper: clarity, realistic experiments and weaker assumptions.
rfa1's praise of clarity is a judgement, not a checkable factual claim that was wrong.
aRng's 6 is in the accept range, and aRng still disputed wording after the rebuttal.
Neither committee refused promised fixes; aRng asked for details in the paper but did not withhold credit on that ground.
No reviewer's stated stance diverged from the score.
rfa1 posted late but is on the record; no off-record reviewer was used.
B's chair adopted the confidence-4 rfa1's verdict of 'clear', while A's chair took the density that aRng and N9bU reported as the main shortcoming.
No silent raise against the review text; raises came with stated reasons.
No chair set aside a silent low score; the silent reviewer, rfa1, was a high scorer and counted.
rfa1's 9 rests on no detailed, checked reading, and no reviewer in either committee argued the case in detail.
No reviewer admitted a partial reading while claiming high confidence.
No reviewer contested the causal framing from another tradition.
B's meta-review only says 'It is my pleasure to recommend acceptance' and quotes two reviewers; it gives no reason for the oral.
Neither committee checked novelty against Zhang et al. (2020) in detail; both took the comparison at face value.
No meta-review misstated final positions toward a lower decision.
No reviewer raised a narrow-audience or venue concern.
A's lowest reviewer, aRng, did not misread the paper; the misreading N9bU raised to 7.
No new experiments were shown to one committee; B's xor example and identifiability argument are explanations.
The reverse holds: B's high-confidence reviewer was the outlier high score, and the chair followed it.
No objection arrived after the response period closed.
B's four 7s match A's mean of 7.0; the gap is one outlier rating, not general leniency.
No reviewer judged the headline claim overstated.

reasoning: The two committees saw the same paper and the same weaknesses; without Reviewer_rfa1's thinly argued, late, unengaged 9, B's mean equals A's 7.0. B's chair quoted rfa1, mentioned no weakness, and gave no case for the oral, while A's chair named clarity the main shortcoming. Existing reasons R02, R03, R09, R12 and R30 cover the B side; R08 and R24 cover the opposite clarity verdicts; R07 covers the one-sided issues; R17 covers N9bU's low-confidence raise in A. No cause in this pair falls outside the existing set, so no reason is added.
